Model assumptions

Erlang C: one FIFO queue, Poisson arrivals, exponential handling times, no abandonment or chat concurrency. Scheduled agents become available after shrinkage. Theoretical modeled service level, not observed SLA. Costs are synthetic scheduled labor cost, not total economic cost.

Methodology & interpretation

Demand and AHT multipliers apply to each interval. For interval contacts V and AHT H, offered load A = V × H / 1800. Available agents = floor(scheduled × staffing multiplier × (1 − shrinkage)). The Erlang C waiting probability is calculated using a numerically stable recursive Erlang B intermediate. Modeled service level at threshold t is 1 − P(wait) × exp(−(N − A) × t/H), for N > A. Required agents are the smallest integer meeting both the service-level target and 85% maximum occupancy. Required scheduled headcount is approximated by ceiling(required available / (1 − shrinkage)). Aggregate service level is weighted by scenario offered contacts. Incremental scheduled labor cost is calculated per 30-minute interval from scheduled headcount difference, not from hypothetical immediately achievable hires. Forecast error and causal impact cannot be established from these synthetic scenarios.
Created for interview preparation. 16,128 generated records · 112 days × 3 regions × 3 queues × 16 half-hours. Not affiliated with Google. No private operational data.
